items.title: Eric Brown Interview, 1969-10-26
items.q: during the war, Max Kaminsky visited Australia, and they got to play with him.

ctx.x: We are going to have a special two-hour session of the program this evening, devoted to music from Australia, from the land down under. And we have with us tonight our special guest commentator, Mr. Eric Brown. And he is going to fill us in on some of the details of the music we're going to be listening to from Australia. We'll be getting to our first selection in just a moment. We'd like to welcome to Speakeasy Junction this evening, Mr. Eric Brown, who is going to tell us a little bit about the music we're…

OK, Ron. First of all, I'm not a musician. I'm a record collector. And I come from Melbourne, which is on the southern coast of Australia, and it's Australia's second biggest city with a population of about two and a half million. It's also the centre of Australian jazz. It's been disputed at times, but it always comes back that most of the jazz is occurring in Melbourne. One of the main reasons for this is because of a jazz band called Graham Bell. Graham Bell is fairly well known in America with some of the…

Let me ask you one thing before we get to the recording itself. Graham Bell is from Melbourne, is that correct? That's correct, yeah. And that was his base of activities when he was active back in the 30s and 40s.
